decisionMeaning: Historical P0 selection of one docking candidate for P1 is retained; the current implementation uses Dockview. P0/P1 comparison and recorded source/desktop results remain historical evidence, not fresh reconciliation checks or complete packaged integration/release proof.

capabilities.modelSerialization: LiOS canonical Project/Session/pane state + Dockview geometry-only serialization

candidates.runtimeShape: Open-source React docking layer over dockview core; upstream package advertises tabs, groups, grids, splitviews, drag/drop, floating panels and serialization.
reasons: Closes the exact current LiOS gaps: arbitrary docking, tab groups and floating panels.
React 18 is supported without forcing a frontend framework migration.
Open-source core is MIT and can remain behind LiOS WorkspaceAdapter.
Selecting one candidate avoids shipping two competing workspace state models.

candidates.runtimeShape: Model-driven multi-tab docking manager with splitter, drag/drop, popout/floating and serialization.
reasons: Capable alternative, but parallel POCs would violate the one-workspace-system convergence rule.
Dockview is the selected P1 candidate because its workbench/docking model maps more directly to the planned Living Workspace.

legacyAlternativeReview: FlexLayout's P0 docking non-selection is not a license rejection or a completed broader SI mechanism/repurposing/challenger analysis. That review remains pending; no competing workspace state authority or second docking installation is permitted.

p1AcceptanceCriteria: Packaged Electron works offline with no upstream cloud dependency.
Existing LiOS Project/Session/Workspace state remains canonical and round-trips losslessly.
Keyboard navigation and accessibility are at least as strong as the current workspace.
Drag/drop docking and tab groups materially improve Living Workspace without default cockpit clutter.
Measure and record renderer startup, memory and bundle impact against an explicit approved release budget.
Saved layouts survive restart and schema migration.
No enterprise/proprietary feature is required for the selected open-source implementation.
FlexLayout is not installed alongside Dockview; only one docking implementation survives the P1 POC.
p0Conclusion: Historical P0 decision: select Dockview open-source core as the sole P1 docking candidate and do not introduce a second workspace manager. Current-main implementation and outstanding packaged evidence are recorded in p1Conclusion and packagedElectronAcceptance.
p1Conclusion: Dockview OSS core remains the Living Workspace renderer behind LiOS-owned WorkspaceAdapter/state, with react-resizable-panels as mobile/maximized fallback. FlexLayout docking and Dockview Enterprise remain excluded; broader alternative mechanism review is pending. Recorded P1 source checks passed, but packaged Dockview interaction/performance/accessibility and P14 release qualification remain open. SP-01/SP-04/SP-07 acceptance must separately record a real integrated MSJ, applicable target execution, no fake success, regression protection and exact commit/build/target/journey/checks/limitations evidence; none is inferred from this benchmark.
